current_fact.fact_text: In 2002, Space Shuttle Endeavour lifted off on mission STS-111 to ferry the Expedition 5 crew to the International Space Station, quietly marking a human endurance milestone: astronaut Franklin Chang-Díaz became only the second person ever to fly in space seven times. The mission was a delicate orbital relay, swapping whole crews and tonnes of cargo in the weightless crossroads above Earth.

queue.fact_text: On 5 June 2024, Boeing’s Starliner capsule finally flew humans for the first time, carrying astronauts Barry Wilmore and Sunita Williams to the ISS after years of delays and test flights. The mission turned a troubled prototype into a working spacecraft, ushering in a new era of private crewed vehicles sharing Earth orbit.

queue.fact_text: In 1991, Space Shuttle Columbia launched STS-40, the first dedicated Spacelab life sciences mission, turning the orbiter into a flying biology lab. Scientists studied how microgravity affects circulation, balance, bones, and even tiny organisms, using space to probe the basic rules of living bodies.

episode.title: Morning Drops #42 - The Joy Of Learning
episode.description:
Hosted by Yasmin, this Morning Drop explores learning as a lifelong process, focusing on persistence, repetition, and the emotional landscape that comes with challenging oneself over time.

Through personal stories and scientific insights, the episode looks at how learning reshapes the brain, generates joy through effort, and why progress often arrives after confusion and frustration. It reflects on the so-called delayed pleasure effect, the role of dopamine in motivation, and how curiosity and learning support long-term wellbeing.

The episode also questions our cultural relationship with failure and invites a softer, more realistic approach to learning, one that accepts mistakes as part of growth and sees persistence as a quiet form of strength.

Mood: reflective, grounded, quietly hopeful
Music genre: alternative rock, hip hop, electronic, neo-soul, drill

A space to listen slowly and stay with the process.

queue.match_reason: A shuttle turned into a life-science classroom in orbit echoes this episode’s curiosity about how science and learning reshape our bodies and brains.

queue.fact_text: On a June evening in 1956, Elvis Presley premiered his single "Hound Dog" on The Milton Berle Show and caused a cultural shockwave simply by moving his hips. The brief TV performance alarmed censors and delighted teenagers, crystallizing rock and roll as something dangerous, physical, and impossible to ignore.

episode.title: Morning Drops #36 - Women of Rock

Distortion, rhythm, freedom.

queue.fact_text: In 2015, a magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck Ranau in Sabah, Malaysia, sending landslides down Mount Kinabalu and trapping climbers on its slopes. It was the strongest quake in Malaysia in four decades, a reminder that even seemingly gentle, tourist-loved mountains can move with sudden violence.

episode.title: Morning Drops #45 - It Can't Rain Forever
episode.description:
In this first broadcast of 2026, Gaia returns from the vivid landscapes of Morocco to open a space for reflection. This episode navigates the delicate transition between closing a significant chapter and stepping into the new year. It explores the concept of constancy amidst change, celebrating the grounding force of friendship and the creative sanctuary that is Sedna FM.

The musical selection mirrors this journey, moving from the orchestral depth of changing seasons into the golden warmth of psychedelic soul. It recalls memories of Swiss mountains and unexpected downpours, reminding us that shared optimism can weather any storm.

Take a moment to breathe in the new morning and listen deeply.

Mood: Reflective, Warm, Transitional, Hopeful
Music genre: Classic Rock, Psychedelic Soul, Pop Rock, Soft Rock

queue.match_reason: A mountain shaken by an earthquake and landslides pairs with an episode about weathering storms and finding resilience in changing landscapes.

queue.fact_text: Back in 1888, the Río de la Plata region between Argentina and Uruguay trembled in one of the strongest earthquakes ever recorded there, despite being far from major plate boundaries. Buildings rocked in Buenos Aires and Montevideo, proof that even "quiet" continental interiors can store deep tectonic surprises.

queue.fact_text: On 5–6 June 2012, Venus slipped across the face of the Sun in a rare astronomical alignment, a tiny dark disc sliding on a blinding star. Such transits come in pairs separated by more than a century; the next won’t arrive until 2117, making this one a once-in-many-lifetimes sunrise for skywatchers.

queue.fact_text: In 1947, U.S. Secretary of State George Marshall stood at Harvard and proposed what became known as the Marshall Plan: a massive program of economic aid to rebuild war-torn Europe. Beyond money, it was a bold bet that recovery, cooperation, and shared prosperity could be a stronger peace treaty than punishment.

queue.fact_text: Tropical Storm Allison made landfall on the Texas coast in 2001 and then refused to leave, looping and stalling over Houston. It never reached hurricane strength, yet its days of relentless rain caused catastrophic flooding and over $5 billion in damage, showing how slow, soaking storms can be more dangerous than dramatic wind.

episode.title: Evening Flows #00 - Introduction to evening flows

Let the music lead the way - enjoy the trip!

queue.fact_text: In 2000, the city of Kisangani in the Democratic Republic of the Congo became the battlefield of the so‑called Six-Day War, a brutal showdown between Ugandan and Rwandan forces during the wider Second Congo War. For nearly a week, artillery duels shattered streets and neighborhoods, leaving large parts of the city destroyed in a conflict far from most headlines.

queue.fact_text: On 5 June 1995, physicists in Boulder, Colorado, coaxed atoms into behaving like a single "super-atom" and created the first Bose–Einstein condensate. At temperatures barely above absolute zero, thousands of atoms overlapped into one quantum state, turning an abstract prediction into a ghostly new state of matter you can almost see.

Over the years it would help discover hydrothermal vents, study Titanic’s wreck, and reveal entire ecosystems thriving in the dark, turning the deep sea from mystery into a living laboratory.

The mystery has haunted Finnish culture for decades, inspiring books, songs, and theories about what really happened in the pre-dawn darkness.

queue.fact_text: In 2003, a ferocious heat wave gripped parts of Pakistan and India, pushing temperatures beyond 50 °C (122 °F) in some regions. queue.fact_text: On 5 June 1984, the Indian Army launched Operation Blue Star, sending troops and armored vehicles into the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar, the holiest site in Sikhism. The operation, aimed at militants inside, left heavy casualties and deep trauma, reshaping Indian politics and Sikh identity for generations.

episode.title: Morning Drops #44 - Residente
episode.description:
In this edition of Morning Drops, Yasmin navigates the complex geography of René Pérez Joglar, known to the world as Residente. His story is not just a musical evolution; it is a timeline marked by resistance, lyrical obsession, and a relentless search for identity.

From the gated streets of Trujillo Alto to the global stage, we explore how a restless mind transformed into the voice of a generation. The selection moves through the textures of his life: hearing the raw energy of his early rebellion, the sharp precision of his political critique, and finally, the fragile silence of his most personal confessions.

It is a study in duality. We witness the rapper who dismantles giants and the son who misses his mother. It is a soundscape that proves that sometimes, the loudest revolution happens inside.

Mood: Raw, Revolutionary, Introspective, Honest
Music genre: Latin Alternative, Hip Hop, Urban, World

episode.title: Morning Drops #27 - Nomophobia

An invitation to rethink how we connect and disconnect.
